claims.text: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, down a concentration gradient, as a result of their random movement, and it needs no energy from respiration. Other things being equal the rate tends to be faster with a steeper gradient, a shorter distance, a larger surface area and a higher temperature; cell surface membranes share the same basic phospholipid bilayer, so the speed of crossing differs between cells because of distance, surface area and gradient, not membrane thickness.

claims.text: Active transport is the movement of particles through carrier proteins against their concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration, using energy from respiration (ATP); it slows if respiration is blocked. Concentration figures alone do not show it: evidence needs movement against the gradient together with evidence of energy use, such as uptake falling when respiration is blocked.

claims.text: In endocytosis the cell surface membrane surrounds material and pinches off as a vesicle inside the cell; in exocytosis a vesicle fuses with the cell surface membrane and releases its contents outside. Both need energy from respiration. Neither is osmosis, which is the movement of water down a water potential gradient and encloses nothing in a vesicle.
